title: Machine learning guides a near-infrared Mo/Sb halide phosphor
summary: A regression model trained on experimental and theoretical data guided Mo/Sb/Br co-doping for a lead-free near-infrared phosphor. The authors report synthesizing Cs₂Zr(Cl₀.₄₆Br₀.₅₄)₆:12%Mo⁴⁺/3.6%Sb³⁺, with emission near 920 nm, internal quantum efficiency of 92.4%, and external quantum efficiency of 65.9% under the reported conditions. Its measured intensity was about 20% higher than the authors’ orthogonal-design comparator. A separate diffusion model was used for image reconstruction demonstrations; this does not establish clinical diagnostic performance. Earlier composition-level prior art and independent replication remain open.
organization: Guangxi University; South China University of Technology

source_review.scope: Primary indexed publisher article and NLM publication metadata; abstract/results, model roles, online date and measured outcomes.

evidence.tested: Authors report synthesis and optical characterization of the predicted composition, LED device testing, and separate imaging demonstration.
evidence.unknown: Study-specific efficiency/intensity results; earlier independent reports and composition-level priority remain unverified; imaging is not clinical diagnostic validation.
evidence.ai_role: A model trained on experimental/theoretical data predicted co-dopant concentrations for researchers to synthesize and test; a separate diffusion model reconstructed imaging outputs.
